results.summary_before: This project is a ring oscillator built from a chain of 21 SkullFET inverters, producing a square wave output. It provides four output pins with the fundamental frequency and divided versions (divide-by-2, 4, and 8). The oscillator is expected to run at approximately 148.6 MHz based on simulation. Testing requires an oscilloscope connected to one of the output pins.
results.summary: This project is a 3-bit up/down counter with reset, enable, load, and up/down control signals. When reset is low the output is zero, when load is low the input data is loaded, and when count enable is high the counter increments or decrements on each positive clock edge. It is written in Verilog and provides three data output bits. Testing uses a 7-segment display and driver with resistors to confirm counting.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design is a modern implementation of the Manchester Baby, the first stored-program computer, with an 8-bit data path and control signals for the PTP interface. It exposes data in and out, stop lamp, RAM read/write, and debug controls, and can be driven from a microcontroller such as the official devkit or a Raspberry Pi Pico. A serial mode reduces the number of required GPIO pins. The design is notable as a historical reimplementation intended for education and demonstration.
